title: Constructive scalar field theory on the lattice: phi^4, Ising and their scaling limits
summary: Single-site measures (phi^4, Gaussian, Ising) and the Griffiths-Simon class; finite-volume Gibbs measures of ferromagnetic pair interactions; Griffiths, FKG, random-current, Lebowitz, Gaussian, Simon-Lieb and Messager-Miracle-Sole inequalities; the free-boundary infinite-volume state, two-point function, susceptibility and critical point; reflection positivity, Gaussian domination and the infrared bound on the torus with Ising long-range order in d >= 3; random fields indexed by test functions, Schwinger functions, Gaussian fields and Wick's law; reachable random fields and the reachability of the Gaussian free field. Marginal triviality in d >= 4 is owned by the downstream ConstructiveFieldTheoryPhi4PartII.

targets.name: IsAdmissible
targets.statement: A Borel probability measure rho on R is admissible if exp(c*phi^2) is rho-integrable for every real c; evenness of rho is Mathlib's MeasureTheory.Measure.IsNegInvariant (rho.neg = rho).
hypotheses: rho a probability measure on R

api.name: isAdmissible_iff_integrableExpSet
api.statement: rho is admissible iff integrableExpSet (fun phi => phi^2) rho = univ.

api.name: integrable_exp_quadratic
api.statement: Admissible rho integrates exp(c phi^2 + h phi) for all real c, h, hence every polynomial.

api.name: closure
api.statement: Admissibility is preserved by scaling phi -> s phi, finite convex combinations and tilting by exp(a phi^2 + h phi) with renormalisation.

api.name: pi_exp_sum_sq
api.statement: For finite V, the integral of exp(c sum_x phi_x^2) against rho^{tensor V} equals (integral of exp(c phi^2))^|V| < infinity.

api.name: of_bounded_support / of_superquadratic_density
api.statement: Bounded support, or a density bounded by C exp(-psi) with psi(phi)/phi^2 -> infinity, implies admissible.

api.name: of_exp_pow
api.statement: If integral of exp(|phi|^alpha) is finite for some alpha > 2 then rho is admissible.

api.name: odd_moment_eq_zero
api.statement: An even measure with finite n-th absolute moment has zero n-th moment for n odd.

tests.name: dirac_admissible
tests.statement: delta_a is admissible with integral of exp(c phi^2) equal to exp(c a^2); it is even iff a = 0.

tests.name: gaussian_not_admissible
tests.statement: N(0,1) is not admissible: integral of exp(phi^2/2) is infinite; for two sites with J = 1 the partition function diverges.

tests.name: cauchy_not_admissible
tests.statement: The Cauchy law has no second moment and is not admissible; the law with density proportional to exp(-phi^2 log(1+phi^2)) is admissible but fails Aizenman-Duminil-Copin (2.2) for every alpha > 2.

tests.name: biased_ising_not_even
tests.statement: (2 delta_{-1} + delta_1)/3 is admissible but not even (mean -1/3).

targets.name: phi4Measure
targets.statement: For lambda > 0 and b real, rho_{lambda,b} has density exp(-lambda phi^4 + b phi^2)/z_{lambda,b} with respect to Lebesgue measure, z_{lambda,b} = integral of exp(-lambda phi^4 + b phi^2) in (0, infinity).

api.name: isProbabilityMeasure
api.statement: rho_{lambda,b} is a probability measure with continuous positive density.

api.name: isNegInvariant / isAdmissible
api.statement: rho_{lambda,b} is even and admissible.

api.name: map_smul
api.statement: For s > 0 the image of rho_{lambda,b} under phi -> s phi is rho_{lambda s^-4, b s^-2}.

api.name: moment_two_mul_zero
api.statement: integral of phi^{2k} d rho_{lambda,0} = lambda^{-k/2} Gamma((2k+1)/4)/Gamma(1/4).

api.name: tendsto_ising
api.statement: rho_{lambda,2 lambda} converges weakly to the Ising measure as lambda -> infinity, with sup_{lambda>=1} of integral exp(c phi^2) finite for every c.

tests.name: second_moment_b_zero
tests.statement: integral phi^2 d rho_{lambda,0} = Gamma(3/4)/(Gamma(1/4) sqrt(lambda)) ~ 0.338/sqrt(lambda); integral phi^4 = 1/(4 lambda).

tests.name: double_well
tests.statement: rho_{1,2} has density maxima at +-1 and a local minimum at 0; b > 0 is a double well.

tests.name: sign_convention
tests.statement: The Gaussian member rho_{0,-1/2} (lambda = 0, b < 0) is gaussianReal 0 1; the opposite sign convention would need b = +1/2.

tests.name: ising_no_density
tests.statement: The Ising measure is not absolutely continuous, so density-based identities do not apply to it.

targets.name: isingMeasure
targets.statement: The Ising measure is (delta_{-1} + delta_1)/2 on R; for b < 0 the Gaussian single-site measure gamma_b = rho_{0,b} is gaussianReal 0 (1/(2|b|)).

api.name: isNegInvariant / isAdmissible
api.statement: rho_I is even and admissible.

api.name: gamma_eq_gaussianReal
api.statement: For b < 0, the probability measure with density proportional to exp(b phi^2) is gaussianReal 0 (1/(2|b|)).

api.name: gamma_not_admissible
api.statement: gamma_b is even and not admissible.

tests.name: ising_moments
tests.statement: integral phi^{2k} d rho_I = 1 and odd moments vanish.

tests.name: gamma_half
tests.statement: gamma_{-1/2} = gaussianReal 0 1.

tests.name: gamma_fails_admissible
tests.statement: integral of exp(|b| phi^2) d gamma_b is infinite.

targets.name: gibbsMeasure
targets.statement: For a finite type V, a symmetric J : V -> V -> R and a probability measure rho on R, H_{V,J}(phi) = -(1/2) sum_{x != y} J_{xy} phi_x phi_y, Z_{V,J}(rho) = integral of exp(-H) d rho^{tensor V} in (0, infinity], the triple is stable if Z < infinity, and mu_{V,J,rho} = Z^{-1} exp(-H) rho^{tensor V}.

api.name: isProbabilityMeasure_of_stable
api.statement: mu is a probability measure when the triple is stable.

api.name: stable_of_admissible
api.statement: If rho is admissible every coupling is stable: -H <= (1/2)||J|| sum phi_x^2.

api.name: gibbsMeasure_zero
api.statement: For J = 0, mu = rho^{tensor V}; for V a point, mu = rho; for V empty, mu is the Dirac measure and Z = 1.

api.name: gibbsMeasure_decouple
api.statement: If J vanishes between V1 and V2 then mu is the product of the two Gibbs measures and Z factorises.

api.name: map_relabel
api.statement: For a bijection e : W -> V the image of mu_{V,J,rho} under phi -> phi o e is mu_{W, J o (e x e), rho}.

api.name: tilt
api.statement: Tilting rho by exp(a phi^2) equals adding a sum_x phi_x^2 to -H.

tests.name: two_site_ising
tests.statement: Two Ising sites: Z = cosh J and <sigma_x sigma_y> = tanh J (ordered-pair convention would give tanh 2J).

tests.name: three_site_ising
tests.statement: Three sites, all pairs coupled with J: Z = (e^{3J} + 3e^{-J})/4, <sigma_1 sigma_2> = (e^{3J} - e^{-J})/(e^{3J} + 3e^{-J}), negative for J < 0.

tests.name: gaussian_unstable
tests.statement: Two sites, single-site N(0,1), J = 1: Z = infinity, the triple is unstable.

tests.name: empty_volume
tests.statement: V empty: Z = 1 and mu is the Dirac measure at the empty configuration.

targets.name: gibbsMeasure_integrable_and_symmetric
targets.statement: For admissible rho, finite V and any coupling J: every polynomial and every exp(sum h_x phi_x + c sum phi_x^2) is mu-integrable; every bijection g of V with J_{gx,gy} = J_{xy} preserves mu; for even rho, mu is invariant under phi -> -phi and <phi_A> = 0 for |A| odd.

tests.name: chain_reflection
tests.statement: Ising chain {0,1,2}, J01 = J12 = J: <s0 s1> = <s1 s2> = tanh J, <s0 s2> = tanh^2 J.

tests.name: non_automorphism
tests.statement: J01 != J12 breaks the reflection: tanh J01 != tanh J12.

tests.name: non_even
tests.statement: (delta_0 + delta_1)/2 on one site: <phi> = 1/2, so the spin flip needs evenness.

targets.name: hasDerivAt_gibbs_coupling
targets.statement: For admissible rho, finite V and measurable F with |F| <= C(1 + sum phi_x^2)^k, J -> <F>_{V,J,rho} is C^1 on symmetric couplings with d<F>/dJ_{xy} = <F phi_x phi_y> - <F><phi_x phi_y> (x != y, symmetric direction).

tests.name: two_site_derivative
tests.statement: d/dJ tanh J = 1 - tanh^2 J = <(s_x s_y)^2> - <s_x s_y>^2.

tests.name: derivative_at_zero
tests.statement: At J = 0 and even rho, d<phi_x phi_y>/dJ_xy = (integral phi^2 d rho)^2, which is 1 for Ising.

tests.name: diagonal_direction
tests.statement: The derivative along a diagonal entry J_xx is 0; including the diagonal would give (1/2)<F; phi_x^2>.

targets.name: tendsto_gibbs_of_tendsto_singleSite
targets.statement: If rho_k -> rho weakly and sup_k integral exp(c phi^2) d rho_k < infinity for every c, then rho is admissible and for every finite V, coupling J and continuous F of polynomial growth, Z_{V,J}(rho_k) -> Z_{V,J}(rho) and <F>_{V,J,rho_k} -> <F>_{V,J,rho}; mu_{V,J,rho_k} -> mu_{V,J,rho} weakly.

tests.name: uniform_bound_needed
tests.statement: rho_k = (1 - e^{-k}) delta_0 + (1/2)e^{-k}(delta_k + delta_{-k}) -> delta_0 but Z(rho_k) >= e^{k^2 - 2k}/4 -> infinity for two sites with J = 1, while Z(delta_0) = 1.

tests.name: hard_limit
tests.statement: rho_{lambda,2lambda} -> rho_I with uniform bounds, so two-site <phi_x phi_y> -> tanh J.

tests.name: J_zero
tests.statement: For J = 0 the statement is weak convergence of finite products.

targets.name: gibbsMeasure_gaussian
targets.statement: For b < 0 and a coupling J on finite V: (V,J,gamma_b) is stable iff 2|b| I - J0 is positive definite (J0 = J with zero diagonal), and then mu = multivariateGaussian 0 (2|b| I - J0)^{-1}. For nearest-neighbour J = 1 on V_R and b = -(d + mu^2/2), mu >= 0, the triple is stable, the covariance is (mu^2 - Delta_R)^{-1} with Delta_R the Dirichlet Laplacian, non-decreasing in R, converging to G_mu(x-y) = (2 pi)^{-d} integral e^{ip(x-y)}/(E(p) + mu^2) dp for mu > 0 (all d) and mu = 0 (d >= 3).
hypotheses: for the limit: mu > 0, or mu = 0 and d >= 3

locator.where: lines 266-269; simon-2020-twelve-tales (3.8) lines 960-975; sokal-1982 footnote lines 394-396

tests.name: one_site
tests.statement: One site, J = 0: mu = N(0, 1/(2|b|)) = gamma_b.

tests.name: two_site_gaussian
tests.statement: Two sites, J of either sign: stable iff |J| < 2|b| (det = 4b^2 - J^2, negative for J = -3|b|); <phi_x phi_y> = J/(4b^2 - J^2), <phi_x^2> = 2|b|/(4b^2 - J^2).

tests.name: one_dim_green
tests.statement: d = 1: G_mu(0) = 1/(mu sqrt(4 + mu^2)), diverging as mu -> 0.

tests.name: massless_low_dim
tests.statement: d = 2, mu = 0: the Dirichlet Green function at the origin diverges as R -> infinity.

targets.name: isingBlockMeasure
targets.statement: For N in N, a ferromagnetic coupling K on Fin N and weights q in [0,infinity)^N, rho_{N,K,q} is the law of sum_n q_n sigma_n under mu_{Fin N, K, rho_I}.

locator.where: Definition 2.1(1), lines 363-373; Figure 1, lines 377-382; weights nonnegative as used at line 2031

api.name: isNegInvariant / finite support / isAdmissible
api.statement: rho_{N,K,q} is even, finitely supported in [-sum q, sum q], admissible.

api.name: degenerate_cases
api.statement: N = 0 or q = 0 gives delta_0; N = 1, q = (s) gives (delta_{-s} + delta_s)/2.

api.name: independent_sum
api.statement: The law of a sum of independent Ising-block variables is an Ising-block measure.

api.name: blockSpin_representation
api.statement: For finite V, ferromagnetic J and rho = rho_{N,K,q}, mu_{V,J,rho} is the image of mu_{V x Fin N, Jtilde, rho_I} under sigma -> (sum_n q_n sigma_{x,n})_x with Jtilde = K within blocks and J_{xy} q_n q_m between blocks.

tests.name: griffiths_trick
tests.statement: N = 2, q = (1/2,1/2), K12 = (ln 2)/2 gives the uniform measure on {-1,0,1}.

tests.name: mixed_signs
tests.statement: q = (1,-1), coupling K: law (1-eps) delta_0 + (eps/2)(delta_2 + delta_{-2}) with eps = 1/(1+e^{2K}); for K > (ln 2)/2, eps < 1/3 and the single-site Lebowitz inequality fails.

tests.name: block_two_site
tests.statement: V = {x,y}, J, N = 1, q = (s): <phi_x phi_y> = s^2 tanh(J s^2), equal to the direct computation.

tests.name: trivial_block
tests.statement: q = 0 gives delta_0.

targets.name: GriffithsSimonClass
targets.statement: rho is in the Griffiths-Simon class iff it is a weak limit of the nonnegative-weight Ising-block measures of 2.1 and integral exp(|phi|^alpha) d rho < infinity for some alpha > 2; growth is imposed on the limit.

locator.where: Definition 2.1(2) and (2.2), lines 374-386; full-class continuity, lines 1982-1985 and 2019-2022; nonnegative weights as in 2.1

api.name: isingBlock_mem
api.statement: Every Ising-block measure is in the class; so are rho_I, delta_0, uniform on {-1,0,1}.

api.name: mem_even_admissible
api.statement: Members are even by weak closure and admissible because c phi^2 - |phi|^alpha is bounded above for alpha > 2.

api.name: closure
api.statement: Closed under phi -> s phi, allowing a smaller exponent between 2 and alpha, and under weak limits of members with sup_j integral exp(|phi|^alpha) d rho_j < infinity for a common alpha > 2.

api.name: gibbs_limit
api.statement: For every member rho, finite V and ferromagnetic J there exists an Ising-block sequence eta_k -> rho weakly such that mu_{V,J,eta_k} -> mu_{V,J,rho} weakly and expectations of every continuous polynomially bounded F converge. This full-class finite-volume transfer includes choice/tail control of approximants; it does not assume uniform superquadratic moments of arbitrary weak approximants (lines 1982-1985, 2019-2022). One sequence must serve any prescribed finite collection of finite ferromagnetic systems simultaneously, including V and its subregions.

tests.name: gaussian_excluded
tests.statement: N(0,1) is a weak limit of Ising-block measures (CLT) but integral exp(|phi|^alpha) dN(0,1) = infinity for alpha > 2.

tests.name: lebowitz_test
tests.statement: (1-eps) delta_0 + (eps/2)(delta_1 + delta_{-1}) with eps < 1/3 is even admissible but not in the class (fails integral phi^4 <= 3 (integral phi^2)^2).

tests.name: phi4_member
tests.statement: Every phi^4 measure is a member (2.3); gamma_b is not.

tests.name: bad_approximation_of_zero
tests.statement: Independent X_N = sum sigma_i/(sqrt(N) log N), N >= 3, have variance 1/log(N)^2 -> 0 but exponential alpha-moments >= 2^(1-N) exp(N^(alpha/2)/log(N)^alpha) -> infinity for every alpha > 2. Constant delta_0 approximants have those moments 1.

tests.name: finite_volume_transfer
tests.statement: The same sequence on one and two sites gives the one-site second moment s^2 and two-site moment s^2 tanh(J s^2); at s=0 these moments are 0 and the zeroth moment is 1. The phi^4 approximants of 2.3 satisfy 1.4 by their uniform tails.

targets.name: phi4Measure_mem_griffithsSimon
targets.statement: For lambda > 0 and b real, rho_{lambda,b} is in the Griffiths-Simon class: with c = (12 lambda)^{-1/4} and g_N = 1 + 2 b c^2 N^{-1/2}, the law rho_N of c N^{-3/4} sum_{n<=N} sigma_n under the Ising measure on Fin N with K_nm = g_N/N converges weakly to rho_{lambda,b} and sup_N integral exp(|phi|^alpha) d rho_N < infinity for alpha in (2,4).

locator.where: pp. 145-164; also aizenman-duminilcopin-2021 lines 392-406, simon-2020-twelve-tales lines 1019-1030

tests.name: entropy_coefficients
tests.statement: I(m) = sum_k m^{2k}/(2k(2k-1)) has coefficients 1/2 and 1/12, matching lambda = 1/(12 c^4).

tests.name: clt_scaling
tests.statement: Scaling N^{-1/2} with fixed g < 1 gives N(0, 1/(1-g)), not in the class.

tests.name: sign_regimes
tests.statement: b > 0 gives g_N > 1 (supercritical Curie-Weiss, double well); b < 0 needs N > 4 b^2 c^4.

targets.name: griffiths_inequalities
targets.statement: For finite V, ferromagnetic J and even admissible rho: <phi_A> >= 0 and <phi_A phi_B> >= <phi_A><phi_B> for all multi-indices A, B.

locator.where: Theorems 2.1 and 2.3, lines 334 and 515; Lemma 2.4, line 535; sokal-1982 (2.20)-(2.21) lines 414-415; glimm-jaffe-1987 Ch. 4

api.name: ginibre_lemma
api.statement: For even admissible rho and m, n in N, double integral of (x+y)^m (x-y)^n d rho d rho >= 0; multivariate form by factorisation.

tests.name: two_site
tests.statement: <s_x s_y> = tanh J >= 0 and <s_x s_y; s_x s_y> = 1 - tanh^2 J >= 0.

tests.name: antiferro
tests.statement: J < 0: <s_x s_y> = tanh J < 0.

targets.name: griffiths_monotone
targets.statement: For even admissible rho: <phi_A>_{V,J} <= <phi_A>_{V,J'} for ferromagnetic J <= J'; <phi_A>_{V,J} <= <phi_A>_{V',J'} for V subset V', J' ferromagnetic restricting to J, A supported in V.

tests.name: chain
tests.statement: Chain 0-1-2: <s0 s2> = tanh J01 tanh J12, non-decreasing in both.

tests.name: volume
tests.statement: V = {0,2} uncoupled: <s0 s2> = 0 <= tanh^2 J.

tests.name: non_even_volume
tests.statement: rho = (2 delta_{-1} + delta_1)/3: adding a coupled site moves <phi_0> from -1/3 to -3e^J/(5e^J + 4e^{-J}) < -1/3.

targets.name: fkg_gibbs
targets.statement: For finite V, ferromagnetic J, admissible rho and bounded measurable coordinatewise non-decreasing F, G: <FG> >= <F><G>; also for polynomially bounded non-decreasing F, G.

tests.name: lattice_gas
tests.statement: (delta_0 + delta_1)/2, two sites: <n_x n_y> - <n_x><n_y> = (e^J - 1)/(3 + e^J)^2 >= 0 iff J >= 0.

tests.name: reverse
tests.statement: F increasing, G decreasing reverses the inequality: F = s_x, G = -s_y gives -tanh J <= 0.

tests.name: harris
tests.statement: J = 0: Harris's inequality; one site, F = G = phi: Var >= 0.

targets.name: Current
targets.statement: For finite V and ferromagnetic J: a current is n from unordered pairs of distinct sites to N; sources dn = {x : sum_y n_xy odd}; weight w_J(n) = prod J_xy^{n_xy}/n_xy!; F_B = currents n admitting m <= n with dm = B. Put Z_D = sum_{dn=D} w(n); define the probability law P^D(n) = 1[dn=D] w(n)/Z_D only when Z_D > 0. Z_empty >= 1.

api.name: weight_summable
api.statement: sum_n w_J(n) = prod exp(J_xy).

api.name: random_current_representation
api.statement: Z <sigma_A> = sum_{dn = A} w_J(n), Z = sum_{dn = empty} w_J(n) ((3.3)-(3.5), lines 429-448).

api.name: switching_lemma
api.statement: sum_{dn1=A,dn2=B} F(n1+n2) w w = sum_{dn1=A Delta B, dn2=empty} F(n1+n2) w w 1[n1+n2 in F_B] for F >= 0 (Lemma 3.3, line 474).

api.name: ratio_formula
api.statement: When Z_{A Delta B} > 0, <sigma_A><sigma_B> = <sigma_{A Delta B}> P^{A Delta B,empty}[n1+n2 in F_B], where the law is the product of normalized constrained laws. Unnormalized switching holds for all A,B, including zero normalizers ((3.7)-(3.9), lines 500-507).

api.name: sources_even
api.statement: dn = A requires |A| even; each source is joined to another source by a positive path.

api.name: normalizer_positive_iff
api.statement: Z_D > 0 iff D has even cardinality in every connected component of the graph of strictly positive J edges; pair sources along positive-edge paths for sufficiency.

tests.name: two_site_currents
tests.statement: Even n: cosh J = Z; odd n: sinh J; ratio tanh J.

tests.name: switching_two_site
tests.statement: A = B = {x,y}, F = 1: left sinh^2 J, right cosh^2 J - 1.

tests.name: no_factorial
tests.statement: Dropping 1/n! gives sum J^n = 1/(1-J), divergent for J >= 1.

tests.name: zero_normalizer
tests.statement: Two sites, J=0,D={x,y}: Z_D=sinh(0)=0, no probability P^D; switching A=D,B=empty is 0=0. At J=1,Z_D=sinh(1)>0 and normalized mass=1. Singleton sources always give 0, as do sources in separate positive-edge components with odd parity.

targets.name: lebowitz_gaussian_simonLieb
targets.statement: Ising, finite V, ferromagnetic J: (i) for n >= 1, <sigma_x1...sigma_x2n> <= sum_j <sigma_x1 sigma_xj><prod_{i != 1,j} sigma_xi> for distinct sites; (ii) Gaussian inequality <sigma_x1...sigma_x2n> <= sum over pairings of products of two-point functions (repetitions allowed), n = 2 is Lebowitz U4 <= 0; (iii) Simon-Lieb <s0 sy>_V <= sum_{u in Lambda, v notin Lambda} <s0 su>_Lambda J_uv <sv sy>_V. The same for phi with rho in the Griffiths-Simon class; corollaries <(sum t_x phi_x)^{2n}> <= (2n-1)!! <(sum t_x phi_x)^2>^n for t >= 0 and integral phi^{2n} d rho <= (2n-1)!! (integral phi^2 d rho)^n.
hypotheses: Ising spins, or rho in the Griffiths-Simon class
0 in Lambda subset V, y in V minus Lambda for (iii)
n >= 1 for recursion (i); n = 0 pairing/moment inequalities use empty product 1.

tests.name: single_site_lebowitz
tests.statement: rho_I: 1 <= 3; rho_{lambda,0}: 1/(4 lambda) <= 3 Gamma(3/4)^2/(Gamma(1/4)^2 lambda) ~ 0.3427/lambda; Gaussian: equality.

tests.name: class_needed
tests.statement: (3/4) delta_0 + (1/8)(delta_1 + delta_{-1}): integral phi^4 = 1/4 > 3/16.

tests.name: simon_lieb_chain
tests.statement: Chain 0-1-2, Lambda = {0}: tanh^2 J <= J tanh J.

tests.name: zeroth_moment
tests.statement: n=0: pairing and Gaussian moment inequalities give 1=1. The recursion selecting x_1 requires n>=1.

targets.proof_route: Any source-conditioned probability in a proof requires its positive normalizer; zero cases use unnormalized switching. Full GS transfer uses the theorem in 2.2, not bare weak continuity.

targets.name: messager_miracleSole
targets.statement: Finite V, even admissible rho, ferromagnetic J, involution R of V with fixed set V0 and V minus V0 = V+ disjoint-union V-, R(V+) = V-, J_{Rx,Ry} = J_xy and J_xy >= J_{x,Ry} for distinct x, y in V+: for multi-indices A, B supported in V+ union V0, <phi_A phi_B> >= <phi_A phi_{R(B)}>. The hypotheses hold for nearest-neighbour J on R-invariant V and R a coordinate reflection in x_i = a (a in Z/2) or a diagonal reflection in x_i +- x_j = a (a in Z).

tests.name: open_chain
tests.statement: {0,1,2,3}, R(x) = 3-x: tanh J >= tanh^2 J and 1 >= tanh^3 J.

tests.name: crossing_stronger
tests.statement: Only J02 = J13 = K: <s0 s1> = 0 < tanh K = <s0 s2>.

targets.name: phi4_ibp_and_uniform_bounds
targets.statement: (a) For lambda > 0, b real, finite V, coupling J, x in V: 4 lambda <phi_x^4> = 1 + 2b <phi_x^2> + sum_{y != x} J_xy <phi_x phi_y> under mu_{V,J,rho_{lambda,b}}, and <d_x F> = <F (4 lambda phi_x^3 - 2b phi_x - sum_y J_xy phi_y)>. (b) max_x <phi_x^2> <= M = [(2b_+ + ||J||) + sqrt((2b_+ + ||J||)^2 + 16 lambda)]/(8 lambda), uniformly in V. (c) For rho in the Griffiths-Simon class, ferromagnetic J and t >= 0: <exp(sum t_x phi_x)> <= exp(<(sum t_x phi_x)^2>/2), and <exp(a|phi_x|)> <= 2 exp(a^2 <phi_x^2>/2).
hypotheses: rho in the Griffiths-Simon class and J >= 0 for (c)

tests.name: single_site_ibp
tests.statement: One site, J = 0, b = 0: <phi^4> = 1/(4 lambda), matching 0.2.

tests.name: bound_value
tests.statement: M(lambda,0,0) = 1/(2 sqrt lambda) >= 0.338/sqrt lambda.

targets.name: freeCorrelation
targets.statement: For translation-invariant finite-range ferromagnetic J on Z^d, even admissible rho and a finitely supported multi-index A: <phi_A>_{J,rho} = lim_R <phi_A>_{V_R,J,rho} in [0, infinity], a non-decreasing limit.
hypotheses: J translation invariant, finite range, J >= 0

api.name: exhaustion_independent
api.statement: Any increasing exhaustion of Z^d by finite sets gives the same limit.

api.name: symmetries
api.statement: Translation invariance, invariance under elements of W_d preserving J, vanishing for |A| odd.

api.name: inequalities_pass
api.statement: Griffiths I, II and, for the Griffiths-Simon class, Lebowitz, Gaussian and Simon-Lieb hold in the limit.

api.name: monotone_J
api.statement: Non-decreasing in J.

api.name: finite_of_uniform
api.statement: Finite if all even single-site moments are bounded uniformly in R and x.

tests.name: ising_chain
tests.statement: d = 1 Ising: <s0 sx> = tanh^{|x|} J for all R >= |x|, so the limit is tanh^{|x|} J.

tests.name: other_exhaustion
tests.statement: W_n = {-n,...,2n} gives the same limits.

tests.name: trivial
tests.statement: rho = delta_0: every positive-total-degree correlation is 0 and the zeroth correlation is 1; A=0 gives 1 and A=2 delta_x gives 0. At J=0 limits are products of single-site moments.

targets.name: infiniteVolumeLaw
targets.statement: Under sup_R sup_{x in V_R} <exp(a|phi_x|)>_{V_R} < infinity for some a > 0: finite-dimensional laws under mu_{V_R} converge weakly; there is a unique probability measure mu_{J,rho} on R^{Z^d} with these marginals, moments <phi_A>_{J,rho}, invariant under translations, J-preserving W_d and phi -> -phi, independent of the exhaustion. The condition holds for bounded-support rho, for phi^4 measures, and for Griffiths-Simon rho with uniformly bounded <phi_x^2>.

api.name: marginal
api.statement: Finite-dimensional marginals of mu_{J,rho} are the weak limits.

api.name: moments
api.statement: integral phi_A d mu_{J,rho} = <phi_A>_{J,rho}.

api.name: invariance
api.statement: Translation, symmetry and spin-flip invariance.

tests.name: ising_markov
tests.statement: d = 1 Ising: stationary two-state Markov chain with P(same) = (1 + tanh J)/2.

tests.name: J_zero
tests.statement: J = 0: mu = Measure.infinitePi rho.

tests.name: determinacy_needed
tests.statement: Without exponential moments, moment convergence does not identify limits (log-normal and its Stieltjes perturbations share moments).

tests.name: fkg_limit
tests.statement: Finite-volume 3.3 passes by uniform integrability to continuous polynomially bounded increasing cylinders: F=G=phi at one Ising coordinate gives 1>=0; independent distinct coordinates give 0>=0.

targets.name: twoPointFunction
targets.statement: S_{rho,J}(x) = <phi_0 phi_x>_{J,rho} in [0, infinity]; chi(rho,J) = sum_x S(x) in [0,infinity]; beta_c(rho,J) = sup{beta >= 0 : chi(rho, beta J) < infinity} in [0, infinity].
hypotheses: J translation invariant finite range ferromagnetic

locator.where: (5.1), lines 1017-1020; sokal-1982 line 470 and Proposition 2.1, line 574

api.name: basic
api.statement: S >= 0, S(-x) = S(x), S(x) <= S(0) when finite, S positive definite.

api.name: monotone_beta
api.statement: S and chi non-decreasing in beta; {beta : chi < infinity} is an interval containing 0; chi(rho,0) = integral phi^2.

api.name: simon_lieb
api.statement: For Griffiths-Simon rho: S(y) <= sum_{u in Lambda, v notin Lambda} <phi_0 phi_u>_Lambda J_uv S(y - v).

api.name: truncated_susceptibility
api.statement: chi_L = sum_{x in Lambda_L} S(x).

tests.name: ising_chain_chi
tests.statement: d = 1 Ising: chi = (1+t)/(1-t), beta_c = infinity.

tests.name: trivial
tests.statement: rho = delta_0: chi = 0, beta_c = infinity; J = 0: chi = integral phi^2.

tests.name: high_temperature
tests.statement: Ising Z^d: Simon-Lieb with Lambda = {0} gives chi <= 1/(1 - 2dJ), so beta_c >= 1/(2dJ).

targets.name: twoPoint_axis_monotone
targets.statement: For nearest-neighbour J >= 0 on Z^d and even admissible rho: the reflection inequality holds in infinite volume for coordinate and diagonal reflections; S(n e_i) non-increasing in n >= 0; S((||x||_inf,0)) >= S(x) >= S((||x||_1,0)); S(x) >= S(y) when ||y||_inf >= d ||x||_inf.

tests.name: ising_chain
tests.statement: d = 1: tanh^n J non-increasing.

tests.name: J_zero
tests.statement: J = 0: S = <phi^2> at 0, 0 elsewhere.

layers.title: Reflection positivity and the infrared bound on the torus

targets.name: periodicGibbs
targets.statement: On T_L = (Z/2LZ)^d, L >= 1: J^per_xy = J #{(j,+-) : y = x +- e_j}; mu^per_{L,J,rho} = mu_{T_L, J^per, rho}; S^_L(p) = sum_x e^{ip.x} <phi_0 phi_x>^per for p in (pi/L)Z^d cap (-pi,pi]^d.

api.name: invariance
api.statement: Invariant under translations of T_L, W_d, and phi -> -phi for even rho.

api.name: fourier_positive
api.statement: S^_L(p) = |T_L|^{-1} <|sum phi_x e^{-ipx}|^2> >= 0, real and even.

api.name: diagonalise
api.statement: sum_x sum_j (phi_x - phi_{x+e_j})^2 = |T_L|^{-1} sum_p E(p) |phi^(p)|^2.

tests.name: L1_torus
tests.statement: L = 1, d = 1: coupling 2J, <s0 s1> = tanh 2J, S^(0) = 1 + tanh 2J, S^(pi) = 1 - tanh 2J.

tests.name: symbol
tests.statement: E vanishes only at p = 0; E((pi,...,pi)) = 4d.

targets.name: reflectionPositive_and_chessboard
targets.statement: Reflection positivity of mu^per through vertex hyperplanes and (J >= 0) edge hyperplanes: <f conj(f o R)> >= 0 for bounded measurable f of one half; chessboard estimate |<prod f_v(phi_v)>|^{|T_L|} <= prod_w <prod_v f_w(phi_v)>.

tests.name: two_site_rp
tests.statement: L = 1, d = 1: matrix proportional to [[e^{2J}, e^{-2J}],[e^{-2J}, e^{2J}]], PSD iff J >= 0.

tests.name: trivial_chessboard
tests.statement: All f_v = 1: equality.

tests.name: product
tests.statement: J=0: edge reflections give |E f|^2; vertex reflections give E |E(f | fixed spins)|^2. At d=1,L=2,R(x)=-x,Ising,f=phi_0, the vertex form is 1 while |E f|^2=0 (Proposition 2.14, line 1331).

targets.name: gaussianDomination
targets.statement: Z(h) <= Z(0) for all h on T_L, Z(h) = integral exp(-(J/2) sum_x sum_j (phi_x + h_x - phi_{x+e_j} - h_{x+e_j})^2) prod rho~(d phi_x), rho~ = e^{dJ phi^2} rho; equivalently <exp(J (phi, Delta h))> <= exp(-(J/2)(h, Delta h)).

tests.name: two_site_gd
tests.statement: L = 1, d = 1 Ising: Z ~ 2e^{-Ju^2} + e^{-J(2+u)^2} + e^{-J(2-u)^2}, second derivative at 0 is -4J + e^{-4J}(32J^2 - 4J) <= 0.

tests.name: lebesgue_equality
tests.statement: Separate Gaussian-gradient example with Lebesgue measure on the connected torus: pin phi_0=0 and take J>0; shifting by h-h_0 yields Z(h)=Z(0)<infinity. Two vertices,J=1: integral exp(-(x-u)^2) dx=sqrt(pi); unpinned integral is infinite. Outside probability a-priori setting (lines 1633-1648).

tests.name: constant_h
tests.statement: h constant: Z(h) = Z(0).

targets.name: infraredBound
targets.statement: For p in Lambda*_L minus {0}: E(p) S^_L(p) <= 1/J; J <(phi, -Delta h)^2> <= (h, -Delta h) for real h; sum rule <phi_0^2> = |T_L|^{-1} sum_p S^_L(p); for d >= 3, |T_L|^{-1} sum_{p != 0} 1/E(p) -> I_d = (2 pi)^{-d} integral dp/E(p).

tests.name: two_site_ir
tests.statement: L = 1, d = 1 Ising: 4J(1 - tanh 2J) <= 1, max ~0.557 near 2J ~ 0.64; the constant 1/(4J) printed in Aizenman-Duminil-Copin (5.9) fails at J = 0.375 (1.46 vs 0.67).

tests.name: gaussian_sharp
tests.statement: Gaussian torus field: E(p) S^(p) = E(p)/(2(|b| - dJ) + J E(p)) -> 1/J as |b| -> dJ.

targets.name: longRangeOrder_ising
targets.statement: For d >= 3, Ising, J > 0: liminf_L <(|T_L|^{-1} sum_x sigma_x)^2>^per >= 1 - I_d/J; for admissible rho, liminf_L (|T_L|^{-1} S^_L(0) - <phi_0^2>^per_L) >= -I_d/J.

tests.name: low_dim
tests.statement: d = 1, 2: I_d = infinity, no conclusion; the d = 1 chain has no long-range order.

tests.name: weak_coupling
tests.statement: J <= I_d: the bound is vacuous.

layers.title: Random fields, Schwinger functions and Gaussian fields

targets.name: RandomField
targets.statement: A random field on R^d over (Omega, P) is T : C_c(R^d) -> Omega -> R, each T_f measurable, with T_{af+bg} = a T_f + b T_g P-a.s. for all f, g, a, b; its law is the image of P on R^{C_c(R^d)} (product sigma-algebra); equality up to finite-dimensional distributions is equality of laws.

locator.where: (1.4), line 56, and footnote 2, lines 183-187; glimm-jaffe-1987 Ch. 6

api.name: law_eq_iff_fdd
api.statement: Equal laws iff all finite-dimensional laws agree; an equivalence relation.

api.name: realise
api.statement: A projective, linear family nu_F on R^F is the fdd family of a random field, unique up to fdd (canonical coordinates under the StochasticCalculus §1.1 limit).

api.name: transport
api.statement: For linear l : C_c -> C_c, (T_{l f}) is a random field (W_d, translations, dilations); negatives, scalar multiples, independent sums.

tests.name: zero_and_deterministic
tests.statement: T = 0 and T_f = integral f h (h locally integrable) are random fields with Dirac fdd laws.

tests.name: white_noise
tests.statement: White noise with E[T_f T_g] = integral fg exists (6.3).

tests.name: absolute_value
tests.statement: T_f = |integral f| is not linear: T_{-f} = T_f.

targets.name: schwingerFunction
targets.statement: For a random field with all moments, M_n(f_1..f_n) = E[prod T_{f_i}]; a locally integrable S_n on (R^d)^n with M_n = integral S_n prod f_i(x_i) dx is an n-point Schwinger function; decay (1.10): for every eps > 0 there is r with |S_2(x,y)| <= eps for a.e. |x - y| >= r.

api.name: moment_multilinear
api.statement: M_n symmetric, multilinear, depends only on the law.

api.name: schwinger_ae_unique
api.statement: Two n-point Schwinger functions agree a.e.

api.name: symmetric_ae / positive
api.statement: Schwinger functions are a.e. symmetric; integral f S_2 f = E[T_f^2] >= 0.

api.name: decay_null_set
api.statement: (1.10) is invariant under null modifications and equivalent to pointwise decay of a representative.

tests.name: deterministic_field
tests.statement: T_f = integral f h: S_n = prod h(x_i); for h = exp(-|x|^2), S_2 <= exp(-|x-y|^2/2) satisfies (1.10); for h = 1 it fails.

tests.name: white_noise_no_S2
tests.statement: White noise has no S_2: it would vanish a.e. off the diagonal, contradicting E[T_f^2] = integral f^2.

tests.name: gff_kernel
tests.statement: The GFF of 7.4 has S_2 = G_m(x-y)/C_m(1_Q,1_Q); in d = 1, G_m = e^{-m|x|}/(2m).

targets.name: gaussianProcessOfKernel
targets.statement: For any type I and symmetric positive semidefinite K : I -> I -> R there is a centred process X with IsGaussianProcess and E[X_i X_j] = K(i,j), unique in law; if I is a real vector space and K bilinear, X is a.s. linear; hence for PSD symmetric bilinear C on C_c(R^d) a centred Gaussian random field with covariance C exists, unique up to fdd.

api.name: covariance_determines
api.statement: A centred Gaussian process is determined in law by its covariance.

api.name: linear_images
api.statement: Linear images of Gaussian fields are Gaussian.

tests.name: bivariate
tests.statement: I = Fin 2, K = [[1,r],[r,1]], |r| <= 1: bivariate normal with correlation r.

tests.name: brownian
tests.statement: K = min(s,t) on [0,infinity): Mathlib's BrownianReal.projectiveFamily marginals; integral fg on C_c gives white noise.

targets.name: isGaussianProcess_iff_wick
targets.statement: A random field with all moments and E[T_f] = 0 is a generalised Gaussian process iff M_{2n+1} = 0 and M_{2n} = sum over pairings of products of M_2; if moreover S_2 exists then S_{2n} = G_n[S_2] and odd Schwinger functions vanish.

tests.name: random_sign
tests.statement: T_f = eps integral f h: M_4 = (integral fh)^4 != 3 (integral fh)^4.

tests.name: centring_needed
tests.statement: T_f = integral fh + W_f is Gaussian but M_1 != 0 violates Wick's law as stated.

targets.name: rescaledLatticeField
targets.statement: T_{f,L,Sigma}(phi) = Sigma^{-1/2} sum_{x in V} f(x/L) phi_x for L >= 1, f : R^d -> R, finite V subset Z^d, Sigma >= 0; finite block second moment (variance for even rho) Sigma^(R)_L(rho,J) = <(sum_{x in Lambda_L} phi_x)^2>_{V_R,J,rho} for R >= L, a stable triple, and every coordinate square integrable under the Gibbs law; 0 <= Sigma^(R)_L < infinity.
hypotheses: Expectations require stability and integrable coordinate squares; normalization Sigma is finite real, zero allowed with T=0.

api.name: linear
api.statement: Linear in f and phi; depends on f only on L^{-1}V.

api.name: hyperoctahedral
api.statement: T_{f o g} (phi) = T_f(phi o g^{-1}) for g in W_d and g-invariant V; equivalently T_f(phi o g) = T_{f o g^{-1}}(phi).

api.name: covariance
api.statement: Under the coordinate-square integrability hypothesis, <T_f T_g> = Sigma^{-1} sum f(x/L)g(y/L)<phi_x phi_y>; a covariance identity for even rho.

api.name: indicator_normalised
api.statement: For a stable law with integrable coordinate squares, <T_{1_Q,L,Sigma}^2>=1 when Sigma=Sigma^(R)_L>0, a second moment and a variance for even rho.

api.name: blockVariance_monotone
api.statement: Sigma^(R)_L non-decreasing in R for even admissible rho, J >= 0; zero only for rho = delta_0.

tests.name: independent_spins
tests.statement: J = 0, Ising: Sigma = (2L+1)^d and <T_f^2> -> 2^{-d} integral f^2.

tests.name: chain_block_variance
tests.statement: d = 1, L = R = 1, Ising: Sigma = 3 + 4t + 2t^2.

tests.name: delta_zero
tests.statement: rho = delta_0: Sigma = 0 and T = 0 by the junk convention.

tests.name: hyperoctahedral_direction
tests.statement: d = 2, L = 1, Sigma = 1, V = {0, +-e_1, +-e_2}, g the rotation (x_1, x_2) -> (-x_2, x_1), f = 1_{e_1}: T_{f o g}(phi) = phi_{-e_2} = T_f(phi o g^{-1}); the identity with g on both sides would give phi_{e_2}, differing for phi = 1_{e_2}. If g^2=id the two candidate formulas agree for every f,phi; for g=-I,f=1_{e_1},phi=1_{-e_1} both give 1.

targets.name: IsReachable
targets.statement: A reachability scheme: rho_n in C, J_n >= 0, L_n -> infinity, R_{n,m} >= L_n with R_{n,m} -> infinity in m, each nearest-neighbour triple stable with every coordinate square integrable, so 0 <= Sigma_{n,m} < infinity; Sigma=0 gives T=0; it converges if for every finite F subset C_c(R^d) the laws of (T^{n,m}_f)_{f in F} converge weakly in m to nu^n_F and nu^n_F -> nu_F in n; a random field is C-reachable if its fdd laws are the nu_F of a convergent scheme.
hypotheses: C a set of probability measures on R

api.name: mono_class
api.statement: C subset C' implies C-reachable implies C'-reachable.

api.name: stability
api.statement: Stability and coordinate-square integrability are automatic for admissible members (1.1-1.2) and for Gaussian gamma_b satisfying 1.5; b <= -d J_n suffices on boxes.

tests.name: white_noise_reachable
tests.statement: rho_n = rho_I, J_n = 0: white noise with covariance 2^{-d} integral fg.

tests.name: delta_zero_class
tests.statement: C = {delta_0}: only the zero field.

tests.name: telegraph
tests.statement: d = 1, rho_I, tanh J_n = e^{-c/L_n}: the random telegraph field kappa^{-1/2} integral f X is reachable and non-Gaussian.

tests.name: finite_second_moment
tests.statement: At J=0 and N block sites, Ising gives Sigma=N, centered Gaussian variance v gives Nv, delta_0 gives 0 and T=0. Standard Cauchy gives Z=1 but its sum has scale N and infinite second moment; excluded from schemes.

targets.name: reachable_structure
targets.statement: Every convergent scheme has a reachable field, unique up to fdd (limits projective and linear); if C consists of even measures, Phi and -Phi have the same law and existing odd moments vanish; reachable fields are W_d-invariant; E[T_f(Phi)^2] <= liminf_n liminf_m <(T^{n,m}_f)^2>.

tests.name: d1_reflection
tests.statement: d = 1: T_{f(-.)} has the law of T_f; for the telegraph field this is reversibility.

tests.name: non_even_class
tests.statement: C = {(delta_0+delta_1)/2}, J = 0: reachable field T_f = 2^{-d} integral f, not symmetric.

tests.name: strict_variance
tests.statement: rho_n = (1-p_n) rho_I + (p_n/2)(delta_{a_n} + delta_{-a_n}), p_n = |Lambda_{L_n}|^{-2}, a_n^2 = 1/p_n: lattice variances -> 2^{-d} integral f^2, limit variance 2^{-d-1} integral f^2.

targets.name: gffCovariance
targets.statement: C_m(f,g) = integral conj(F f(xi)) F g(xi) / (4 pi^2 |xi|^2 + m^2) d xi (Mathlib Fourier transform), finite and PSD for m > 0 (all d) and m = 0 (d >= 3); the Gaussian free field of mass m is the centred Gaussian random field with covariance C_m(f,g)/C_m(1_Q,1_Q). The same Fourier integral is also evaluated at the block indicator 1_Q in L^1 intersect L^2; pointwise radial kernel formulas apply for x != 0, and the value at 0 does not affect integrals.

locator.where: Section 2.3, lines 620-721; frohlich-1982 lines 266-269; glimm-jaffe-1987 Ch. 6

api.name: psd
api.statement: C_m is symmetric, positive semidefinite and finite on C_c(R^d). Non-increasing in mass in quadratic-form order, not on arbitrary cross terms.

api.name: position_space
api.statement: Consume the analytic continuum Green kernels, Fourier agreement, exterior decay (m>0) and decaying massless radial kernel (m=0,d>=3) from RelativisticQuantumFieldTheory §7.1; prove C_m(f,g)=integral integral f(x)G_m(x-y)g(y), identifying the C_c-indexed covariance here.

api.name: normalisation_finite
api.statement: 0 < C_m(1_Q,1_Q) < infinity.

tests.name: d1_kernel
tests.statement: d = 1: C_m(f,g) = integral integral f(x) e^{-m|x-y|}/(2m) g(y); C_m(1_Q,1_Q) = 2/m^2 - (1 - e^{-2m})/m^3. At m=1,xi=0 multiplier=1, G_1(1)=exp(-1)/2 and block normalization=1+exp(-2). C_2(f,f)<=C_1(f,f), whereas cross terms with g=-f reverse that inequality.

tests.name: massless_d1
tests.statement: d = 1, m -> 0: C_m(1_Q,1_Q) ~ 2/m diverges.

tests.name: d4_singularity
tests.statement: d = 4: G_m(x) ~ 1/(4 pi^2 |x|^2) near 0, locally integrable on R^4.

targets.name: gff_reachable
targets.statement: For d >= 1 and m > 0, and for d >= 3 and m = 0, the Gaussian free field of mass m is reachable from {gamma_b : b < 0} with J_n = 1, b_n = -(d + m^2/(2 L_n^2)), arbitrary L_n -> infinity and R_{n,m} -> infinity.

locator.where: Section 2.3 and Lemma 2.2, lines 620-721; frohlich-1982 lines 266-269; simon-2020-twelve-tales lines 960-975

tests.name: dirichlet_kernel
tests.statement: The transform of 1_Q on the lattice is a product of Dirichlet kernels converging to prod 2 sin(q_j)/q_j.

tests.name: d4_instance
tests.statement: In d = 4 the field has S_2 satisfying (1.10), a non-vacuous instance of the field hypotheses of downstream goal 8.1 from the Gaussian class.

suppliers.what: Kolmogorov extension for an arbitrary index set of standard Borel coordinates: existence and uniqueness of the projective limit of a projective family of probability measures (used for random fields indexed by C_c(R^d) and Gaussian processes with prescribed kernel).
Wick-Isserlis mixed-moment formula for centred multivariate Gaussian vectors with positive semidefinite covariance.

Analytic Green kernels of -Delta+m^2: heat integral, Fourier multiplier with 4 pi^2 normalization, local integrability and exponential exterior decay for m>0,d>=1; decaying radial massless kernel and Fourier agreement for m=0,d>=3. Probability law, block normalization and lattice reachability remain here.

consumers.what: Owns statements and proofs of downstream goals 8.1-8.2; consumes Layers 0-7. Owns current intersection estimates, tree and improved tree bounds, spectral representation, boundary-condition comparison, infinite-volume and sliding-scale infrared bounds, uniform local integrability and applications to OS reconstruction.
